newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president wants to revalue currency.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president wants to revalue currency.

text.p: Ecuador's Presdient Abdala Bucaram said Tuesday his government would implement a plan to revalue the sucre, the Ecuadorean currency, against the U.S. dollar.

"We are preparing a plan to strengthen the Ecuadorean currency. All my life I have said that the worst thing that can happen is a devaluation. I am setting out to revalue our currency, that is to say, a higher value," Bucaram told the press.
Analysts have said that such a revaluation would be unsustainable as long as Ecuador suffers from inadequate flows of foreign capital into the country and unstable domestic prices.

Still, Bucaram said: "I am a definite supporter of a higher value for our currency. Japan is trying to have a stronger yen than the dollar, Britain is attempting to have a stronger pound than the dollar and Ecuador has 3.350 sucres to a dollar," Bucaram said.
The president added that he did not know whether the currency would continue being called the sucre.

Ecuador's new government is now in the final stages of preparing of an economic program to be presented on November 16. On Wednesday, the government is expected to send its 1997 budget proposal to Congress.
